grammarChart.affirmative:
I/You/We/They have <past participle>.
He/She/It has <past participle>.
grammarChart.negative:
I/You/We/They have not (haven't) <past participle>.
He/She/It has not (hasn't) <past participle>.
grammarChart.question:
Have I/You/We/They <past participle>?
Has He/She/It <past participle>?

explanation: The Present Perfect tense connects past actions to the present. It is formed with 'have/has' + past participle (e.g., 'I have studied'). It indicates actions that happened at an unspecified time before now, ongoing actions, or experiences relevant to the present.
keyRules: 1. Unspecified past time (no exact date/year): 'I have visited Paris.'
2. Life experiences: 'She has visited three countries.'
3. Ongoing actions with present relevance: 'They have lived here since 2010.'
4. Recent actions with present results: 'He has just left.'
5. Changes over time: 'The climate has changed dramatically.'
azarNotes: Use 'already', 'yet', 'ever', 'never', 'just', 'so far': 'Have you already eaten? I haven't finished yet.'
No specific time words (e.g., 'yesterday') with Present Perfect: ❌ 'I have eaten yesterday.' ✅ 'I ate yesterday.'
Past actions with present consequences: 'She has broken her leg (and can't walk now).'
commonMistakes: Confusing Present Perfect with Past Simple: ❌ 'I have went to the store.' ✅ 'I went/I have gone to the store.'
Incorrect use of 'ago': ❌ 'I have seen her two days ago.' ✅ 'I saw her two days ago.'
Forgetting past participle: ❌ 'She has run fast.' ✅ 'She has run quickly.'
Mixing tenses unnecessarily: ❌ 'I have eating lunch.' ✅ 'I have eaten lunch.'
ieltstip: Use Present Perfect to discuss recent changes, lifelong experiences, or actions affecting the present. In IELTS Writing/Speaking, it demonstrates advanced grammar control (e.g., 'Many people have become more health-conscious in recent years').

quiz.question:
Choose the correct sentence:
A) I have watched that movie last night.
B) She has watched that movie last night.
C) We have watched that movie yesterday.
quiz.answer: None (all incorrect). Present Perfect cannot use 'last night/yesterday' with no specific time allowed.

quiz.question: Correct the mistake: 'He has broke his leg.'
Fill in the blank: 'Have you ____ (she) to Paris before?'
Is this correct? 'They have lived here since 2015.'
quiz.answer: Yes (correct use of ongoing action with present relevance)

quiz.question: Rewrite using Present Perfect: 'I bought a new car last month.'
quiz.answer: I have bought a new car last month. (Note: Technically incorrect, but sometimes accepted in informal speech. Better: 'I have bought a new car.' or 'I bought a new car last month.')
